display.title: The Sound of the Shofar: Why We Blow It on Rosh Hashanah
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains the mitzvah of shofar on Rosh Hashanah: a wake-up alarm that crowns Hashem as our King and calls us to teshuvah.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week before Rosh Hashanah. Uncle Yossi introduces the sound of the shofar, the ram's horn that the Torah commands us to blow on Rosh Hashanah, 'a day of sounding the shofar'. As the Rambam says, the Torah gives no reason for the mitzvah, since it is a heavenly decree, but it hints at many lessons. Above all, the shofar is like an alarm that wakes a person from sleep: it reminds us that a new year has begun, that on this day we proclaim Hashem our King and ourselves His servants, our Father and ourselves His children, and that we must ask Him to inscribe us in the Book of Life. We do teshuvah, regret our wrongdoings and resolve to learn more Torah and keep more mitzvos, and Hashem in His kindness grants us a good and sweet year.
display.lesson: The shofar is a wake-up call: crown Hashem as King, do teshuvah, and resolve to do better in the new year.

date.note: From episode 245, 'the last Tuesday of this year' before Rosh Hashanah 5747. The talk also aired in episodes 139, 291, 342, 441 and 544.

sources_cited.note: 'It shall be a day of sounding the shofar for you.'
A heavenly decree with a hint: the shofar says 'wake up, sleepers'.
